source.title: GSEM: Graph-based Self-Evolving Memory for Experience Augmented Clinical Reasoning

observations: The first inspected public pre-submission repository commit already wires GSEMMultiStartNoFillAgent as Ablation 4 and imports a dedicated retriver_multi_start_no_fill implementation.

The normal multi-start retriever force-fills the starting experience whenever a traversal selects nothing; the no-fill ablation's documented sole difference is to preserve the empty set instead of backfilling that starting experience.

The paper's published retrieval ablation reports entity-recall, embedding-recall and multi-seed traversal rows, with GSEM at 94.22 diagnosis, 94.59 treatment and 34.00 MedBullets, but it does not report a no-fill versus forced-fill row.
No committed numerical output artifact bound to GSEMMultiStartNoFillAgent was found in the inspected public surfaces during this run.

protocol_inference.claim: Empty retrieval/no-memory is an intentional separable design factor in this clinical memory system, but its numerical efficacy cannot be inferred from implementation existence alone.
protocol_inference.evidence_strength: exact public pre-submission design-factor evidence; no bound outcome evidence
protocol_inference.canonical_effect: supports the legality of EMPTY_MEMORY_IS_A_VALID_RUNTIME_ACTION but does not establish its performance effect

scope_limits: The exact commit used for paper evaluation is not bound by a published manifest in the evidence inspected here.
The no-fill factor lacks a published quantitative outcome in the paper's Table 3 and no bound repository result was found.
The workflow requires external LLM/model execution and clinical benchmark data; it is not an end-to-end scheduled-Chat zero-external-executor parity mechanism.
